title: Mediated Interactions between Fermi Polarons in the Strongly Interacting Regime
authors: Renato Pessoa, S. A. Vitiello, Luis A. Peña Ardila
abstract: Mediated interactions between quasiparticles lie at the heart of Landau Fermi-liquid theory, yet their behavior in the strongly correlated regime is not fully understood. Motivated by recent experiments [Nat. Phys. 20, 68--73 (2024)], we investigate mediated interactions between quasiparticles emerging from a Fermi sea---Fermi polarons---using zero-temperature quantum Monte Carlo methods. Our main result is that the Landau interaction between polarons remains repulsive in the strongly interacting regime for any coupling strength in the polaronic branch, in contrast to the downward trend observed experimentally near resonance. Deep in the short-range universal regime, our results are insensitive to the microscopic details of the interaction potential, providing robust evidence for the sign of the ground-state induced interaction. In addition, we determine the real-space interaction between static impurities, recovering a Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY)-like behavior at weak coupling and the nonperturbative Born-Oppenheimer result at strong coupling. More broadly, our results establish a microscopic benchmark for how Landau quasiparticle interactions survive beyond the perturbative regime of strongly correlated quantum matter.
summary: This theoretical study uses Quantum Monte Carlo simulations to calculate the mediated interactions between Fermi polarons in strongly correlated quantum matter. The authors demonstrate that the fundamental repulsive nature of the interaction survives into the strongly coupled regime, providing a robust theoretical benchmark. This work is vital for interpreting experimental measurements in ultracold Fermi gases by separating intrinsic many-body physics from finite-temperature or short-range artifacts.
main_problem: The study investigates the behavior of mediated interactions between quasiparticles (Fermi polarons) in the strongly correlated regime, where standard Landau Fermi-liquid theory breaks down.
main_result: The calculated Landau interaction between polarons remains robustly repulsive in the strongly interacting regime, contradicting some experimental trends, and the methodology successfully recovers RKKY-like behavior at weak coupling.
method: The research employs zero-temperature Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) methods, utilizing Jastrow-Slater trial wave functions, to calculate ground-state properties.
model_or_system: The system models fermionic impurities (polarons) interacting within a surrounding Fermi sea (bath), using potentials like Pöschl-Teller or zero-range models to parameterize the interaction strength.
key_observables: Landau interaction parameter ($ ar{f}$), real-space mediated interaction potential $V(R)$, and single polaron energy ($\epsilon_0^{\downarrow}$).
important_parameters: Coupling strength ($X$), impurity concentration ($C$), and the comparison between weak-coupling (RKKY) and strong-coupling (Born-Oppenheimer) limits.
main_assumptions: Calculations are performed at zero temperature ($T=0$), and the analysis distinguishes between the mobile quasiparticle response and the fixed-scatterer potential.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the polaron energy vs. coupling strength, the induced interaction vs. coupling strength (showing persistence of repulsion), and the mediated potential $V(R)$ recovering RKKY oscillations at weak coupling.
paper_structure: The paper systematically calculates the polaron energy and the induced interaction using QMC for various potentials, first establishing agreement with LFLT at weak coupling, then pushing into the strongly correlated regime to benchmark the interaction sign and the static impurity potential.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, microscopic, zero-temperature benchmark for understanding how interactions persist beyond the perturbative regime, which is crucial for interpreting complex experimental results from ultracold atomic systems.
